items.title: Court of Justice rules national rent caps compatible with EU free movement of capital
items.source: Council of the EU — press releases (demo)
items.summary: In a judgment delivered today the Court of Justice ruled that national housing rent caps do not breach EU law. The ruling ends a long dispute and is binding on all member states. Landlord associations criticised the decision; tenant campaigners called it historic.

items.title: UK and EU agree youth mobility scheme in principle
items.summary: The United Kingdom and the European Union have reached a political agreement on a youth experience scheme allowing under-30s to live and work across borders. Ministers said it was unprecedented since Brexit. The agreement is binding from 2027.

items.title: Deal on air passenger rights: MEPs secure improved traveller protection
items.summary: Negotiators reached a provisional agreement on new rules that will be binding from 2027. Students and young travellers using budget airlines will see compensation thresholds change. The deal was criticised by consumer campaigners as watered down.

items.title: Commission proposes first-ever EU rules on age verification for social media
items.summary: The Commission unveiled a proposal that would require very large online platforms to verify the age of users. The mandatory scheme would apply to TikTok and Instagram and carry fines of up to 6 percent of global turnover. Digital rights campaigners warned it amounts to surveillance.

items.title: Erasmus+ budget cut by 12 percent in draft MFF, universities warn
items.source: Council of the EU — press releases (demo)
items.summary: Draft multiannual financial framework figures show the Erasmus+ student mobility programme facing a 12 percent reduction. University associations warned it would price out students from lower-income households. The proposal is contested and MEPs have threatened to reject it.
